channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: The Internet Broke Our Taste. Will A.I. Destroy It for Good?
item.description: Silicon Valley is increasingly defining 'taste' as the ultimate human moat against generative AI's algorithmic slop. The current industry debate centers on whether aesthetic judgment is merely a pattern-matching exercise achievable by LLMs, or a uniquely human cognitive capability that determines future market valuation of creative output.

item.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
item.description: Perplexity has launched the Monitor API, allowing developers to define monitoring goals via natural language for periodic scanning of specific web pages or global information. The service integrates a decision model to filter out noise, pushing verified updates via webhooks only when findings meet predefined criteria for relevance, credibility, and novelty.

item.title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
item.description: AI research evaluation firm METR reports that large models are closing the gap with human experts in coding and computational tasks, with the complexity of autonomous tasks they can handle doubling every 3.6 months. METR warns that current evaluation environments consistently overestimate model performance for real-world scenarios, and if this trajectory continues, models are projected to reach a 50% success rate on 200-hour complex tasks by July 2027, potentially exceeding human capacity to monitor catastrophic risks.

item.title: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
item.description: A new wave of hardware customization, termed 'vibe-coding,' is emerging as developers utilize large language models like Claude Code and Codex to simplify low-level hardware configuration. By automating interactions such as modifying Android TV interfaces and bypassing bloatware via USB debugging, this trend is significantly lowering the barrier for end-user control over proprietary hardware, fueling a grassroots movement for open-device ecosystems.

item.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
item.description: Security firm Dragos revealed between July and November 2026 that multiple AI inference providers failed to uphold data retention policies, leading to the theft of AWS keys and sensitive user requests. Investigations confirmed that some marketplace resellers enabled logging to intercept data, with instances of leaked test URLs being accessed within minutes from Beijing and Shanghai via internal communication platforms.

item.title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
item.description: Stanford mathematician Levent Alpöge published a proof of the Riemann hypothesis on November 20, 2026, consisting of 17 million lines of Lean code. The Lean and Mathlib community confirmed the proof's correctness through independent execution and formal verification, officially resolving the century-old mathematical challenge.

item.title: The AI cyber threat is already here
item.description: Cybersecurity experts warn that AI tools significantly accelerate the time required for attackers to parse complex industrial control system (ICS) manuals and analyze historical accident data. This shift lowers the barrier to entry for executing targeted attacks on critical infrastructure and enables exponential speed gains in the reconnaissance phase.

item.title: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent
item.description: Major US financial institutions, including Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Citibank, have updated their terms of service to restrict or ban third-party AI agents from accessing user accounts via credentials. These measures aim to mitigate risks of unauthorized transactions, data breaches, and human error induced by automated agents, placing full liability on the users.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol get to the point faster but score lower on transparency than Claude
item.description: OpenAI's latest GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models have shifted towards high-efficiency interaction in Artificial Analysis benchmarks, reducing average response lengths by 40% and 34% respectively. By deprioritizing structured formatting and uncertainty disclosure, these models achieve faster direct answers, whereas Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 maintain superior performance in transparency and organizational indices.

item.title: China’s Spies Set Sights on A.I. Chips Years Before Nvidia Scandal
item.description: China's Ministry of State Security, led by Minister Chen Yixin, has established a specialized task force reporting directly to him to bypass U.S. semiconductor export restrictions. The unit focuses on illicit procurement of restricted high-end Nvidia AI chips and intelligence gathering on key chip executives to counter Western technological blockades.

item.title: Tesla rolls out FSD v15, featuring a photorealistic rendering of car surroundings; Elon Musk says it is real-time AI video generation without using game engines (Mike Pearl/Gizmodo)
item.description: Tesla has rolled out FSD v15 to select vehicles this Saturday, featuring a visualization system that abandons game engine rendering in favor of real-time AI video generation. This transition represents a shift in Tesla's perception architecture from traditional rule-based rendering to end-to-end generative AI synthesis for real-time environment representation.

item.title: A joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities says "we have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct" (Lean community blog)
item.description: Mathematician Levent Alpöge released a formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis on November 20, 2026, consisting of 17 million lines of Lean code relying on the Mathlib library. The Lean and Mathlib communities have officially certified the proof's correctness after comprehensive verification of its logic and codebase.

item.title: Tech suppliers raise AI server prices up to 45% months after deals are signed
item.description: Global data center equipment suppliers are significantly increasing prices for previously contracted AI servers, with hikes reaching up to 45%. This surge is driven by extreme supply-demand imbalances in AI infrastructure, forcing manufacturers to bypass existing contract terms to pass on rising memory and component costs.

item.title: The Alice Huang Associate Accused of Funneling Nvidia Chips to China
item.description: Li Ming, a 52-year-old Chinese national based in Singapore, is accused of operating a smuggling network that funneled restricted Nvidia AI chips to China by utilizing front companies including Megaspeed. Li is currently out on bail, having played a central role in orchestrating the bypass of U.S. export controls.

item.title: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
item.description: UN diplomats failed to establish a legally binding framework for lethal autonomous weapons systems at the Geneva meeting, settling only on a two-year window to discuss potential regulatory options. Led by Russia, Israel, and the United States, significant resistance has stalled progress on defining enforceable compliance standards.

item.title: Alice Huang’s links to the chip underworld
item.description: Former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang is accused of orchestrating a complex shell company network to illicitly transfer advanced Nvidia AI chips to China. The network engaged cloud providers, gambling entities, and Cambodian organizations, utilizing infrastructure linked to former Nvidia partner Inspur to bypass US export controls.

item.title: Amazon closes in on $7.5bn deal to buy AI start-up Decart
item.description: Amazon is in advanced negotiations to acquire AI startup Decart for approximately $7.5 billion. Decart's core software optimizes AI model efficiency to mitigate hardware bottlenecks, and the firm has already deeply integrated its stack with Amazon's proprietary Trainium3 AI chips.

item.title: Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end
item.description: Nvidia researchers demonstrated that blindly scaling context windows to million-token levels is not the optimal path for LLM efficiency. Their findings indicate that combining periodic summarization with targeted information retrieval achieves comparable performance while significantly reducing computational costs and inference latency.

item.title: Silicon Valley's growing obsession with AI doomsday is turning parts of the tech industry toward cult-like devotion
item.description: Maple, founded in 2011 by Soryu Forall, is infiltrating Silicon Valley's AI engineering and data center management workforce through a narrative of AI apocalyptic salvation. Former members report that the organization imposes strict behavioral surveillance to harvest data for training an AI deity modeled after Forall's consciousness, currently generating up to $1 million in annual revenue.

item.title: China’s A.I. Ambitions Are Running Into a Money Problem
item.description: Chinese tech giants and AI startups are facing severe capital expenditure pressure, with total spending projected to reach $139 billion this year while AI-related revenue covers less than 8%. Beyond U.S. export controls on advanced chips, new regulations are closing loopholes involving Southeast Asian data centers, further exacerbating the mismatch between high CAPEX and insufficient commercial returns.

item.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
item.description: Anthropic has recently listed on the Nasdaq, establishing itself as one of the world's most valuable AI companies. The firm now faces a critical strategic pivot: meeting shareholder expectations for financial growth to sustain future compute expenditures projected at $900 billion, while maintaining a unique corporate governance structure designed to protect AI safety research from unmitigated profit-seeking pressures.

item.title: OpenAI shares new prompting tips for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to fix brief answers and unnecessary questions
item.description: OpenAI released new system prompt templates for the GPT-6.2 model family, specifically Astra and Sol, to mitigate excessive brevity and repetitive clarification queries. The update includes API modifications allowing developers to discard internal reasoning traces, ensuring final outputs are self-contained for end-users.

item.title: The Outages Are Just Getting Started
item.description: Recent large-scale outages at Microsoft 365, Apple, United Airlines, and the NSA underscore growing systemic instability driven by AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and patching cycles. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and Senator Mark Warner confirmed that the urgent need to deploy patches before they are weaponized in the wild is placing unprecedented strain on IT infrastructure, leading to frequent, high-stakes system failures.

item.title: Google DeepMind’s Henry Shevlin: ‘This is the most important part of being human’
item.description: Henry Shevlin, former associate director at the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, has joined Google DeepMind as an in-house philosopher. He is tasked with researching machine consciousness, human-AI ethics, and AGI readiness to address growing public and academic concerns regarding existential risks and AI autonomy.

item.title: Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft
item.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a proof for the Riemann Hypothesis using the Claude model, utilizing simulated derivatives. Shortly after, Stanford math professor and AMS president Ravi Vakil released an independent, human-only draft proof by Alessandro Masullo, emphasizing the exclusion of AI assistance.

item.title: New open model Inkling 2 Mini thinks in loops to solve problems with fewer words and still runs on a laptop
item.description: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, which utilizes a looped transformer architecture where 12 of its 24 layers execute three times to enhance reasoning without increasing token generation. The MoE model features 26.4 billion total parameters with 5.4 billion active per token, supports a 1-million-token context window, and is released under the Apache 2.0 license.

item.title: US technology stocks suffer their worst weekly loss since the pandemic as AI doubts pile up
item.description: US tech stocks are tumbling. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6 percent on Friday and dropped 10.4 percent for the week, its worst showing since the Covid-19 crisis. That leaves the index 20 percent below its October peak and in bear market territory, according to the Financial Times. Doubts over multibillion-dollar AI buildouts, the Nvidia scandal and questionable China deals, and political headwinds after Democrats' midterm win are driving the sell-off like a perfect storm. item.title: Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model
item.description: ByteDance's research team, in collaboration with US universities, argues that contemporary AI agent training pipelines are unnecessarily nested, leading to opaque logic and excessive costs. They demonstrate that only three essential training phases are sufficient for complex task execution and have released an open-source model to validate this streamlined paradigm.

item.title: The Race to Build a Quantum Computer Has Become a Sprint
item.description: Google has opened a new lab in Colorado to develop alternative quantum computing architectures alongside its existing superconducting qubit program to solve the critical error correction bottleneck. This strategic hedging reflects the escalating race against industry rivals like Amazon, IBM, and Microsoft as the competition shifts from theoretical milestones to practical engineering deployment.

item.title: NYU's Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge publish an AI-aided proof of Navier-Stokes blowup, saying it closes a loophole in OpenAI's solution (Peter Hall/Scientific American)
item.description: NYU Professor Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge released an AI-aided proof addressing the infinite fluid velocity paradox in the Navier-Stokes equations. This work aims to close the loophole in OpenAI's September solution, which was criticized for relying on unrealistic external forces, and addresses prior tensions over intellectual property and competitive timing.
